analysis.title: Risk Premium in Pictures: High earnings, higher expectations, how much is already priced in?
key_insights: SG's monthly equity risk premium (ERP) report covers 27 developed and 23 emerging markets. The theme is that investor focus is moving from the pace of earnings growth to its sustainability. Markets with the biggest upgrades to earnings expectations (Korea, Taiwan, US) have generally outperformed, but several reacted negatively to in-line earnings results.

Korea's current earnings trajectory is about five times the level expected a year ago. Taiwan's is nearly double and the US is about 30% higher. 2026 equity gains were about 14% for the US and about 86% for Korea and Taiwan.

Cost of equity has risen sharply even as prices rose. Korea's is about 12% versus about 5.5% a year ago. Korea's ERP rose about 550bps in a year, with earnings revisions adding about +796bps against -146bps from the higher index and -126bps from higher bond yields. SG says these markets offer much better value only if current consensus estimates are delivered.

SG inverts the valuation model to find the long-term growth rate 'g' that current prices need for an 8% annualised return, then compares it with its own 'g' estimate. In local currency, all emerging markets except China and Taiwan need less growth than SG's estimate. In developed markets the peripheral euro-area countries and the UK show the most room for earnings disappointment.

On an 8% USD return hurdle, Taiwan, Japan and Mexico have limited scope for earnings disappointment because prices already embed demanding growth. Korea, Brazil and Indonesia need only modest growth. Peripheral euro-area markets also screen better on this measure.

Cyclically elevated earnings distort the signal. 2027E EPS forecasts for Korea, the US and Taiwan sit well above trend, so valuations may look attractive mainly because earnings expectations are unusually high. Indonesia, China and Germany are nearer cyclical troughs, with forecasts at or below trend.

Reported EPS in many markets has fallen by more than 50% peak to trough over the last 15 years. The US is historically less cyclical but its current forecast looks close to a cyclical peak. Japan is historically more cyclical but appears earlier in the cycle.

Spain, Italy and Korea can absorb the largest 2027E and 2028E EPS cuts while still delivering an 8% return. Korea's required 2027E EPS is still about 3.5 times its latest reported EPS (FY2025), so the apparent margin of safety is overstated by the sharp jump in the earnings trajectory.

Global ERP is 4.0% and the IRR on equities is 8.6%, with consensus EPS growth of 39.0% in 2026e, 16.6% in 2027e and 15.2% in 2028e. The developed-market ERP is 3.8%, emerging markets 5.5%, and Asia 6.1%. US ERP is 3.5%, below its 4.2% average, with a 10Y yield of 5.1%.

Credit versus equity: US equities offer a 2.7% excess return over US IG yield (average 2.8%) and 0.2% over US HY (average -0.9%). Euro equities offer 4.2% over Euro IG (average 4.3%) and 2.2% over Euro HY (average 0.7%). US HY spread over Treasuries is 3.3% versus a 4.8% average, and Euro HY is 2.4% versus 4.3%.

Backtests since 1990 on US assets: ERP/VIX-based equity/bond allocation returned 8.6% annualised with 7.9% volatility and a 1.09 Sharpe ratio, versus 10.9% and 0.71 for 100% equities. Since 1995, a cost-of-capital-weighted four-country ERP allocation (US, UK, Germany, Japan) returned 7.9% with a 0.79 Sharpe versus 7.8% and 0.48 for equal-weighted equities.

Month-on-month, ERP rose in the US (+32bp since Sep 2026 per summary table) and Europe (+21bp), and fell in Brazil (-167bp) and Korea's bond yield context shows cost of capital up 234bp, the largest move among major Asian markets.
earnings_insights: Consensus index EPS growth (estimates, not reported): US 34% 2026e, 18% 2027e, 17% 2028e. Korea 334% 2026e, 36% 2027e, 5% 2028e. Taiwan 65% 2026e, 31% 2027e, 26% 2028e. Japan 23%, 13%, 11%.
Global consensus EPS growth (market-cap weighted estimates): 39.0% 2026e, 16.6% 2027e, 15.2% 2028e. Emerging markets 104.9%, 23.3%, 14.6%. Developed markets 30.5%, 15.7%, 15.3%.

The report notes several markets with the strongest earnings expectations reacted negatively to earnings releases even when reported results were broadly in line with consensus. No company-level figures are given.
Korea's required 2027E EPS for an 8% cost of equity is about 3.5 times its latest reported EPS (FY2025). This is a model output, not a Street estimate.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The consensus earnings trajectory is about five times what was expected a year ago, which drives the jump in implied cost of equity but also raises cyclical-peak risk.
The US earnings trajectory is about 30% above year-ago expectations, and 2027E forecasts screen as near a cyclical peak versus trend.
Earnings expectations are nearly double year-ago levels, and the price already embeds demanding growth on SG's USD-hurdle measure.

trade_ideas.description: Model-based country allocation across US, UK, Germany and Japan weighted by cost of capital, with equity/bond split set by ERP per unit of 1-month realised volatility. Stated country weights: UK 29%, Germany 26%, USA 26%, Japan 19%.
trade_ideas.rationale: Backtested since 1995 at 7.9% annualised return, 10.0% volatility and 0.79 Sharpe, versus 7.8% and 0.48 for equal-weighted equities.

risk_factors: Cyclically elevated 2027E earnings in Korea, Taiwan and the US could mean the apparent cheapness of those markets disappears if earnings revert toward trend.
Historical peak-to-trough EPS declines exceed 50% in many markets, so a consensus cut is a real risk where forecasts sit above trend.
Markets whose implied long-term growth is above SG's estimate (Taiwan, Japan, Mexico on the USD hurdle) have little margin for earnings disappointment.
Negative price reactions to in-line earnings suggest investors are already questioning how long high earnings growth can last.
charts_described: Korea ERP bridge chart shows the start at 251bp, -146bp from the index, -126bp from bond yields and +796bp from earnings, ending at 775bp.
Bar chart of required long-term growth 'g' for an 8% USD return versus latest 'g' across 17 markets, with Taiwan, Japan and Mexico needing the most and Korea, Brazil and Indonesia the least.
Chart of 2027E earnings cyclicality z-score ranks Korea, the US and Taiwan highest and Indonesia, China and Germany lowest.
vol_and_positioning: SG's ERP/VIX indicator ranks the US ERP relative to the VIX within its 1990-to-date range as a percentile to set the equity weight. Backtest since 1990: allocation using ERP/VIX returned 8.6% with 7.9% volatility and a 1.09 Sharpe. ERP only: 9.6%, 11.8%, 0.82. VIX only: 7.7%, 7.9%, 0.98. 50/50: 9.2%, 10.1%, 0.90.

A synthetic indicator of ERP per unit of 1-month realised volatility sets equity weights by country. Applied to the US, UK, Germany and Japan since 1995, it raised the Sharpe ratio versus static equity-only portfolios (0.75 equal-weighted, 0.79 cost-of-capital-weighted, versus 0.48 equity only).

tension_points.bull_case: Korea, with Spain and Italy, can absorb the largest cuts to 2027E and 2028E consensus EPS while still delivering an 8% return, and it needs only modest growth on the USD-return measure.
tension_points.bear_case: Korea's required 2027E EPS is about 3.5 times its latest reported EPS and its 2027E forecast is well above trend (highest cyclicality z-score), so the margin of safety may be overstated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A cut to 2027E and 2028E consensus EPS larger than the implied cut that still leaves an 8% return.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong earnings upgrades in Korea, Taiwan and the US have driven outperformance, and higher cost of equity means better value if consensus is delivered.
tension_points.bear_case: Taiwan, Japan and Mexico have limited scope for earnings disappointment on the USD-return measure, and several high-expectation markets fell on in-line results.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Required long-term growth for an 8% USD return rising above SG's own long-term growth estimate for the market.
